title: Mum called my name. She was dead.

hook_text: Mum called my name from downstairs. She'd been gone six months.

scenes.narration: She had been gone six months. I was alone in Gran's old house up north. The nearest neighbour was a mile away.

shots.prompt: empty bedroom in an old stone cottage at night, single bed, rain on the window

scenes.narration: Gran's notebook lay by the bed. The first page had one rule, underlined twice. If someone calls your name after midnight, don't answer.

shots.prompt: old leather notebook open on a wooden bedside table by candlelight, handwriting blurred and illegible

scenes.narration: It called again. Mum's voice. Soft. Patient. Exactly how she used to wake me for school. Then it came from the other side of my bedroom door.

shots.prompt: closed wooden bedroom door in a dark old house, thin light under it, a shadow of feet

scenes.narration: My mobile lit up. Unknown number. I answered without thinking. Gran whispered. Don't let it know you're awake.

shots.prompt: smartphone glowing in the dark on a quilt, unknown caller screen, blue light

overlays.text: Don't let it know you're awake

scenes.narration: Then I heard her again. Not through the phone. From the kitchen. Downstairs. Gran was down there, whispering to me. Alive. Somehow. In a house she never left.

shots.prompt: long dark hallway of an old house, a thin line of light from a kitchen door at the far end, no person

scenes.narration: So who had been standing behind my door? The handle moved. Slowly. And it started to laugh. Quietly. With Mum's voice. Like it had finally found me.

shots.prompt: bedroom door handle slowly turning in the dark, no person visible

scenes.narration: So tell me. Do you answer it, or stay silent?

shots.prompt: dark old stairwell and hallway of a stone house at night, a faint light under a closed door, no person visible
